value.body: A microbiologist in industry tests raw materials, products, water and the production environment for microbial contamination. Employers include pharmaceutical and vaccine makers, food and dairy companies, cosmetics makers and testing labs. A typical day involves preparing media, running microbial limit and sterility tests, monitoring clean areas and recording results to good manufacturing practice (GMP) standards.

items.label: Common methods
items.value: Culture media, microbial limit tests, sterility tests, environmental monitoring

items.label: Work setting
items.value: Quality-control labs in plants and testing labs

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Freshers usually join as QC microbiology trainees or officers in pharma, food or dairy plants. Many employers prefer an M.Sc, though B.Sc graduates also get trainee roles. Aseptic technique and familiarity with GMP documentation help.

value.title: At a glance
items: Shift work is common in manufacturing QC labs.
Next roles: senior microbiologist, QC or QA lead, validation specialist.
Hospital diagnostic microbiology is a separate track with its own qualification rules.

competition.note: B.Sc (all subjects) graduates in 2023-24 at institutions that reported to AISHE — everyone finishing that degree, not only those entering this role.
